finding: An edge end or a step role that is a list or map (unhashable) makes `in roles` raise TypeError instead of PatternRefused, so a malformed one-off pattern exits 1 with a traceback, not 2.
why: The contract says an edge or step that names a role its record does not define is refused with exit code 2, and main() catches only PatternRefused, OSError and ValueError. Failing input: a one-off pattern with edges [{"from": ["a"], "to": "b", "kinds": ["message"]}] or a step {"name": "s", "roles": [["a"]]}; D-45 leaves value checks of a one-off pattern to the resolver.
fix: Test `isinstance(x, str) and x in roles` (here and at line 200), or wrap the record check so TypeError and KeyError become PatternRefused.
evidence: `if edge.get(end) not in roles:` (line 181); `if role not in roles:` (line 200); main() `except (OSError, ValueError)` (line 388)

finding: The AC-039 'no agent, message or spend limit' check uses the resolver's own RECORD_KEYS as the oracle. Widening RECORD_KEYS to add 'agent-limit' (mutant record-keys-widened) and removing the unknown-record-field refusal (mutant record-unknown-field-off) both left all 73 tests green.
why: The test passes whatever the allowed-key set contains, so it cannot detect a limit field becoming legal, and no test feeds a saved record with an unknown or limit field to the resolver.
fix: Assert against a literal key set in the test, and add a refusal test for a saved record carrying a 'max-agents' field.
evidence: assert set(record) <= resolver.RECORD_KEYS, "no pattern record carries an agent, message or spend limit"

finding: Nothing exercises the path-safety refusals. Replacing resolved_path's unsafe-feature condition (resolver.py:66) with `if False:` and the _role_name condition (resolver.py:89) with `if False:` each left all 73 tests green.
why: The feature id and the role names become file and directory names later, so an untested refusal can regress to path traversal unnoticed.
fix: Add refusal cases for feature ids '', '..', 'a/b' and for role names '..', 'a/b', 'a:b', and for a report target with a path separator.
evidence: resolved_path is only ever called with the constant FEATURE = "feat-x"; no test passes a role or report-target name containing a path separator

finding: A role whose report target is itself, or a report-target cycle (a->b->a), is accepted; its finished message and the implied edges go nowhere useful and the asker never gets a result.
why: The check only requires the target to be a defined role. Failing input: roles {"a": {..., "report-target": "a"}} resolves and writes implied edges a->a and a->a.
fix: Refuse a report target equal to the role, and a report-target cycle, with PatternRefused naming the role.
evidence: `if target and target not in checked_roles:` (lines 122-124) is the only report-target check; _implied_edges (lines 263-265) then emits a->a both ways

finding: Each debate step with no hub appends its own moderator<->debater message edges, so a pattern with 2 hubless debate steps over the same roles writes every edge twice.
why: The resolved team then carries duplicate edges, and a consumer that counts or compares edges sees them twice; the roles merge by name but the edges do not.
fix: Skip an edge already in self.edges before appending (or build the moderator edges once per pattern).
evidence: `self.edges.append({"from": MODERATOR, "to": role, "kinds": ["message"]})` inside the per-step loop (lines 242-243), with no membership test

finding: A pattern that defines its own non-hub role named `moderator` and has a debate step with no hub is refused with 'role moderator has 2 different definitions, in patterns X and X', naming the same pattern twice.
why: The refusal is correct in effect but misleading, because the added moderator is the resolver's, not a second pattern's definition.
fix: Refuse a record-defined role named `moderator` up front in _check_record, naming it as reserved, or let a record's own `moderator` serve the debate.
evidence: `self.merge(MODERATOR, self.moderator, name)` (line 239) hitting `elif known != fields: raise PatternRefused(f"role {role} has 2 different definitions, in patterns {self.owner[role]} and {pattern}")` (lines 256-257)

finding: Implied edges written into the resolved file carry an extra `implied` key and, for an empty report target, `to`/`from` equal to ""; the resolver's own edge check (EDGE_KEYS, role-name membership) would refuse both, so step 0010 cannot re-run `_check_edge` over the file's edges.
why: SDD §4 says the flattened team uses the field names of a pattern data file and adoption rebuilds the team from the file, so a consumer that validates the file with the record rules would refuse a resolver-written file.
fix: State the `implied` key and the empty-string end in the file format (STANDARD.md or the resolver docstring) so step 0010 and adoption read them as written.

criterion: Acceptance: a refused pattern/charter check covers every role; the added moderator is a role
finding: The moderator the resolver adds takes its charter from moderator.md with no presence check, unlike every record role, which _check_role refuses when its charter part is empty.
why: SDD §13 Q54 (1) says the resolver refuses a role with no charter part, so an empty or whitespace moderator.md would start a moderator with only the pattern parts as its charter.
fix: Refuse with PatternRefused, naming the moderator role, when the moderator part is empty after strip; add a test.
evidence: `"charter": (PATTERNS_DIR / MODERATOR_PART).read_text(encoding="utf-8")` in _moderator, with no _text() test, while _check_role has `if not _text(fields.get("charter")): raise PatternRefused(... charter part is missing or empty)` (line 147)

criterion: Acceptance: the pattern standard's record-shape table, the resolver checks the values
finding: STANDARD.md says the resolver checks a role model as `<tier>@<provider>` against PROVIDERS.md tier and provider rows, but the resolver only checks the model is non-empty text.
why: The standard is the schema's one home that agents read when writing a pattern; it states a check that does not exist, so a bad model form is refused only later as an unfillable role.
fix: Reword the row to say the resolver checks only that a model is present and that the caller's fill rule accepts it, or add the form check.
evidence: STANDARD.md:49 `The resolver checks the values:` and :54 `role model | <tier>@<provider>: a tier row of PROVIDERS.md "Model tiers" ...`; resolver.py:149 `if not _text(fields.get("model")):`

criterion: Acceptance: the resolved pattern file carries record version (empty only for a one-off pattern) and source (built-in, saved or one-off)
finding: A pick of 2 or more names writes source "combined" and a null record version, outside the 3-value source set and the one-off-only empty rule of the contract bullet and SDD §4.
why: The deviation is recorded as plan D-56, so it is a two-way door, but a reader of the resolved file (adoption, S-177/SNAP-1) and the 0010 consumer must now accept a fourth source value the SDD does not name.
fix: Keep D-56 and carry the fourth value to the SDD §4 source row and to 0010 (the file's reader), or give the first pattern's source and version the top-level fields.
evidence: `{"pattern-name": "+".join(names), "record-version": None, "source": "combined"}` (line 331); DECISIONS.md D-56 `Supersedes: SDD §4 resolved pattern "source: one of built-in, saved, one-off"`

criterion: changed path matches a ## Scope glob
finding: Commit 03ec150 edits .claude/wiring-ious.md (IOUs for resolve_pattern( and resolved_path(), lines 30-31), a path no ## Scope glob in 0005 lists. Every other changed path is in scope or a run artifact (plan/JOURNAL.md, PLAN.md, DECISIONS.md, investigations/, skipped).

finding: Several input guards are untested. Disabling each left the suite green: empty or non-text session; empty moderator_model; includes that is not a list of names; a record whose name field disagrees with its key; an empty pick list; a non-map `saved`; a non-bool step `debate`.
why: The pick, session and moderator-model refusals are part of the public resolve interface, and the suite pins none of them (mutants session-unchecked, moderator-model-unchecked, includes-shape-off, name-mismatch-off, pick-empty-ok, saved-map-unchecked, debate-type-off survived).
fix: Add one parametrized refusal test over these inputs, asserting the refusal text.

finding: The reporting-duty test loops over every role part plus the moderator part with bare asserts that do not say which part failed.
why: A failing assert shows the shared line but not the role or the moderator part, so triage needs a rerun.
fix: Add the role name to each assert message or parametrize per role.
evidence:
for part in parts:
        assert PROGRESS in part

finding: The one-off check asserts record-version None only on the top-level field. Mutant oneoff-version-kept, which writes a one-off's own record-version into `sources`, survived, because no test inspects `sources` for a one-off.
why: AC 'record version (empty only for a one-off pattern)' and 'keeps the name and version of each source' go unchecked for the one-off source entry.
evidence: assert result.pattern["source"] == "one-off" and result.pattern["record-version"] is None
